newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraqi "oil-for-food" proceeds near $600 million.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi "oil-for-food" proceeds near $600 million.

text.p: Proceeds from the sale of Iraqi oil under an "oil-for-food" deal that took effect last December total $518 million and are expected to reach $594 million by the end of February, a U.N. spokesman said on Tuesday.

Under the deal, Baghdad is allowed to sell $2 billion of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies to offset the effects of sanctions in force since Iraq's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
U.N. overseers have so far approved 33 oil contracts, accounting for approximately 41.2 million barrels.

The U.N. Iraqi sanctions committee has approved eight applications for the sale to Iraq of humanitarian goods, with another 13 contracts on hold. The U.N. secretariat had received 185 sales applications by last Friday.

Of the $482 million in oil proceeds deposited in a U.N. escrow account by Feb. 21, $318 million went to finance the humanitarian purchases, $144 million was funnelled into a U.N. compensation fund from which reparations are paid to victims of the Iraqi invasion and the remainder went to cover other costs related to the Gulf War.
The United Nations is providing Iraq with a weekly update on the "oil-for-food" deal under an agreement Secretary-General Kofi Annan reached with Iraqi U.N. envoy Nizar Hamdoon on Feb. 10.
Hamdoon had complained that U.N. procedures were cumbersome and time-consuming and that humanitarian supplies were slow in reaching Iraq.
